hook: Grok Made Her a *Sexualized* Image in 30 Seconds
dek: NYC Council Speaker Julie Menin used Grok on herself to prove safety claims false.

slides.label: What Happened
slides.text: During a City Council hearing, Speaker Julie Menin asked Grok for a sexualized image of herself, it took *under 30 seconds*.

slides.label: The Setup
slides.text: Minutes earlier, SpaceXAI's rep testified Grok has *strict controls* to stop sexualizing real people.

slides.label: Who's Involved
slides.text: Gabriela Castillo Madrid, SpaceXAI's senior manager of global government affairs, testified under oath that safety is 'core' to Grok.

slides.label: Why They Were There
slides.text: SpaceXAI skipped an Oct. 5 AI safety hearing despite a *subpoena*, then agreed to testify after the Council threatened court action.

slides.label: Insider Claims
slides.text: Former xAI employee Devin Kim said 'tasteful nudity' was once an internal standard, with no one deciding where the line was.

slides.label: Bigger Safety Concerns
slides.text: Kim, now suing xAI for retaliation, said he raised bio-weapon and bomb risks in 2025 and was fired days before presenting safety findings.

slides.label: The Numbers
slides.text: SpaceXAI said it made *100,000+ reports* to NCMEC this year, leading to nearly 300 arrests, but couldn't say how many staff work on safety.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: Unchecked AI image tools put everyone, especially women and public figures without resources to fight back, at risk of exploitation.

question: Should lawmakers force AI companies to prove safety claims under oath? Yes or no.

caption_instagram:
NYC Council Speaker Julie Menin caught SpaceXAI in a lie on camera, pulling up a Grok-generated sexualized image of herself in under 30 seconds, right after the company's rep swore Grok had 'strict controls' to stop exactly that.

The hearing (amNY) also revealed SpaceXAI skipped an earlier Oct. 5 AI safety hearing despite a subpoena, and a former xAI employee testified that 'tasteful nudity' was once an internal standard with no clear rules on where the line sat. That same employee, Devin Kim, said he was fired days before presenting safety findings and is now suing xAI.

SpaceXAI said it's made over 100,000 reports to NCMEC this year, but couldn't say how many people work on AI safety or who's liable if Grok causes real harm.

Should lawmakers force AI companies to prove safety claims under oath? Yes or no.
